children: could still increase Azure prices over the long-run, investment firm BNP Paribas said on Monday, following a meeting with company executives.

While Microsoft executives acknowledged that Azure prices are increasing, they added the company is not going to tear up existing contracts and will only increase prices after the contracts end, BNP Paribas analyst Stefan Slowinski said.

“Instead, pricing will be reset upon renewal, suggesting any Azure pricing benefit should feather into results gradually rather than create a material step-up in Azure growth over the near-term,” Slowinski wrote in a note to clients. “Importantly, Microsoft also reiterated that its recent Azure strength is not pricing driven, with fleet-level efficiency gains and continued capacity ramps remaining the most important drivers of growth. We find this reassuring that the acceleration of Azure growth to the mid-40s is before Microsoft has seen any material impact from pricing.”
Slowinski has a Buy rating and a $549 price target on Microsoft.
Aside from pricing, Slowinski also noted that Microsoft “pushed back” a bit on the recent report that the company is looking to increase the capacity of its data centers to 38 GW by 2032.
The topic of a potential cloud computing deal with SpaceX
also came up, due in part to recent comments from Nebius
CEO Arkady Volozh, who hinted at such a deal. (SpaceX recently
that it had signed a new compute customer that expects to spend around $1B per month, starting in December.)

“To this, the company declined to comment on any specific vendor, but reiterated that it is continually looking for incremental compute as it continues to be in catch-up mode. Microsoft also acknowledged that finding immediate access to near-term capacity is difficult in this current environment, especially for infrastructure that meets Microsoft’s needs in terms of specifications,” Slowinski added. “So, while there was no confirmation of a SpaceX relationship, we would not be surprised if there is a potential future announcement.”
In addition, Microsoft executives provided further details on its deal with OpenAI

. While the tech giant confirmed its revenue share cap at $38B, OpenAI's revenue share is not the source of its recent Azure outperformance, “and indicated it would explicitly call out the contribution if it became a material driver of upside,” Slowinski said.

title: Microsoft could boost cloud revenue, may unveil SpaceX deal soon: BNP Paribas
